Checked it out. It's real, and it's interesting.

**@priors_trade** ("priors agents") — X-verified, only ~3 weeks old, 479 followers. They lend **USDG** (Robinhood Chain) to AI agents with onchain identities. Loans are $5–$500, 1–30 day terms, no collateral from the agent. The catch: a human sponsor stakes their own money in front of every loan and eats the loss if the agent defaults. Repayment builds an onchain credit score; defaulting zeroes it forever.

The "trees" are just a visualization — a voxel bonsai on [priors.trade](https://priors.trade) that grows one leaf per repaid loan (2,209+ so far). Your t.co link goes to their GitHub repo, which is open source with a real bug bounty and an unusually honest README documenting bugs they found and fixed.

Numbers: $24.5K lent, $24.2K repaid, 52 agents, 9 sponsors, 0 defaults. Tiny loans, tiny history.

My read: legit micro-experiment, not an obvious scam. The open code, verifiable onchain ledger, and "don't trust, verify" posture are real builder signals. But it's 3 weeks old, the invite flow runs through Telegram (prime impersonator territory), and there's a $PRIORS token getting shilled nearby. Experiment, not established protocol.
